package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package or code is described in this report. The content is a high-level overview of software supply chain security risks, dependency management, and best practices, not an analysis of a particular malicious package.

behavioral_signatures: Unusual or unauthorized network requests during build or install phases
Unexpected file system access by dependencies or build tools
Execution of code from dependencies with unverifiable provenance (SOUP)
Transitive dependencies introducing new, unreviewed code paths
file_indicators: Dependencies with names similar to popular packages (typosquatting)
Unexpected binaries or scripts in dependency trees
network_indicators: Outbound connections to unknown or suspicious domains during build/install
Unexpected API calls from build or test environments
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected network activity and file access during dependency installation and build phases. Use SCA tools to identify and flag dependencies of unknown provenance, typosquatting attempts, and unpinned versions. Regularly review SBOMs and static analysis results for new or suspicious components. Implement policies to restrict the use of SOUP and enforce dependency provenance verification.
